chunks: From him, from Yusuf ibn al-Sukht, from Ali ibn Muhammad ibn Sulayman, from his father, from Isa ibn Abdullah, who said:

Abdullah was presented with death, so his creditors gathered around him and demanded the debt owed to them. He said, 'I have no wealth with which to give to you, but be pleased with whichever you choose from the two sons of my uncle: Ali ibn al-Husayn (peace be upon him) and Abdullah ibn Ja'far.' The creditors said, 'Abdullah ibn Ja'far is wealthy and delays (payment), but Ali ibn al-Husayn (peace be upon him) is a man with no wealth, truthful, and he is more beloved to us.' [A man] with no wealth, truthful, and he is more beloved to us.

So he sent for him and informed him of the news. He said, 'I guarantee the wealth for you until harvest time,' as a show of kindness, and there was no harvest for him. The people said, 'We are pleased,' and they held him as a guarantor. When the time of harvest came, Allah, Mighty and Majestic, made the wealth available to him, so he paid it.

key_terms.تَجَمُّلًا: As a show of kindness / gesture of goodwill

ai.seo_question: How did Imam Ali ibn al-Husayn (peace be upon him) guarantee a debt without having wealth at the time?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi highlights the virtue of *al-amanah* (trustworthiness) over material wealth, as creditors chose Imam Ali ibn al-Husayn (AS) for his truthfulness despite his lack of immediate funds. The term *tajammul* used for his promise of 'harvest' indicates a rhetorical gesture of goodwill rather than a literal expectation of agricultural yield, emphasizing reliance on divine provision (*rizq*). The narrative concludes with Allah facilitating the means for repayment, illustrating the principle that God supports those who fulfill their obligations with sincerity.

en.hubeali: From him, from Yusuf Bin Al Sukht, from Ali Bin Muhammad Bin Suleyman, from his father, from Isa Bin Abdullah who said,

‘(Death) presented itself to Abdullah, so his creditors gathered around him so they sought the debts which were for them. So he said, ‘There is no wealth with me so I can give it to you, but turn to whoever you like from the son of my uncle Ali<sup>asws</sup> Bin Al Husayn<sup>asws</sup> and Abdullah Bin Jaffer’. So the creditors said, ‘Abdullah Bin Ja’far delays and prolongs (matters), and Ali<sup>asws</sup> Bin Al-Husayn<sup>asws</sup> is a man with no wealth for him<sup>asws</sup>, (but) is a truthful one, and he<sup>asws</sup> is the more beloved of the two to us’.

So he sent for him<sup>asws</sup>, so he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘I<sup>asws</sup> take the responsibility for you for the wealth to a harvest (time)’ as a show of kindness, and there was no harvest for him<sup>asws</sup>. So the people said, ‘You<sup>asws</sup> have pleased us’, and they held him<sup>asws</sup> as a guarantor. So when the time of harvest came, Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Mighty and Majestic Gave him<sup>asws</sup> the (required) wealth, so he<sup>asws</sup> paid it’.
en.sarwar: 7. It is narrated from him (narrator of previous Hadith) from Yusuf ibn al-Sukht from Ali ibn Muhammad ibn Sulayman from his father from ‘Isa ibn ‘Abd Allah who has said the following:

“‘Abd Allah was about to die and his creditors gathered around him demanding payment. He said to them, ‘I do not have any property to pay you but you may choose one of the sons of my uncle, Ali ibn Al-Husayn, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, and ‘Abd Allah ibn Ja’far who will assume responsibility to pay you.’ They said, “Abd Allah ibn Ja’far is a procrastinator and slow to respond. Ali ibn Al-Husayn, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, does not have any properties but is a truthful person and more beloved one of the two to us.’

He then sent someone to inform him of the case, and he said, ‘I assume responsibility to pay you by the time of harvest,’ although he did not have any harvest but he said so to show kindness. The people said, ‘We accept your offer.’ He assumed the responsibility and when time for harvest came Allah, most Majestic, most Glorious, made it possible for him to pay and he did so.”
